page.overview:
Who is Althea?

Althea was a female member of the royal family of Isobe during the Imperial Era. She and her brother Thelan were the children of Lord Hallux. She developed a brief relationship with Jun Sato, a human from Mykapo who had joined the renowned crystal processing school on Isobe. However, it turned out that Sato was part of a smuggling ring, which led him to be banished from Isobe for life, much to Althea's dismay.

Princess Althea was a member of the royal family of Isobe during the Imperial Era, a world that became rich as one of the sole sources of the tynzo crystal, a mineral used in strengthening glass for use in hyperspace. The daughter of Lord Hallux and the sister of Thelan, she had a brief relationship with Jun Sato, a human from Mykapo who had joined the renowned crystal processing school on Isobe. However, Sato had only joined the school as a ruse, actually coming to Isobe after having been recruited to a smuggling ring that stole tynzo crystal and exported it at a lower cost than Isobe, weakening the resource's price. Sato was caught by Isobe's security forces and put on trial. He refused to tell who gave him orders and was banished for life from the planet.

Althea later died between 4 BBY and 2 BBY on Isobe. Her father had a gravestone created that he inscribed himself, carving a tynzo crystal in the shape of a heart to be placed atop her grave. During the inscription process, Hallux and her brother Thelan, accompanied by two guards, were interrupted by the gardener Levier and his droid Gee-Bee, who had apprehended Sabine Wren defacing a statue of Hallux and Sato. Sato, who faced the death penalty for returning to Isobe, revealed to Hallux that it was his son, Thelan, who ran the smuggling ring and had only kept his silence before to protect Althea. Hallux had Thelan arrested and granted Sato one hour to pay his respects to Althea before he was to leave Isobe forever.

Althea was a female Sephi who was thin and had long hair. She was not like other Sephi who held xenophobic views towards outsiders. Her father held her in great esteem, inscribing "Beloved daughter" on her gravestone.
